This Mfa Coming On For Final Hearing This Day,
Rajesh Rai K. J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This Miscellaneous First Appeal is by the appellant/claimant directed against the judgment and award dated 24.07.2018 in MVC No.747/2017 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi, (henceforth referred as 'Tribunal') whereby the Tribunal rejected the claim petition.
Parties to the appeal are referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

03. The facts leading rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that:
On 12.07.2015 at about 1.00 a.m., near Shetty Huda Dhanamma Temple on S.H.
No.10, when the deceased Sharavan Kumar along with his friend Murlidhar were proceeding on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-32/EE- 3943 to Malkhed Cement Company from Sedam, at that time, an unknown vehicle came and dashed to the above said motorcycle due to which the deceased Sharavan Kumar and his friend Murlidhar sustained grievous injuries and Shravan Kumar died on the spot.

In this regard, a complaint came to be registered against the unknown vehicle for the Smt.Akkamma Hugar vs Sri.Devaraj Shetty And Anr on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67106067/
2 offenses punishable under Sections 279 and 304-A of IPC and Section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: As such, the claimant being the mother of deceased filed claim petition before the tribunal claiming compensation.
Though notice served, respondent No.1 remained absence and placed ex parte.
Respondent No.2 filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
05. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
06. In order to substantiate the contention of claim petition, the petitioner was examined as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P.1 to P18.
The respondent No.2-Insurance Company examined its official as RW.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R1.
07. After assessment of oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal rejected claim petition.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the tribunal, the petitioner filed the present appeal.

08. We have heard Smt. Shantabai Patil for Smt. Anita M. Reddy and Lakshmi G.E., learned counsel NC: 2024:KHC-K:3855-DB for the petitioner and Sri S.S. Aspalli, learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
09.

It is the primary contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that, the Tribunal has erred in rejecting the claim petitioner without properly appreciating the evidence and documents available on record.
According to the learned counsel, the death of deceased Sharavan Kumar in the road traffic accident occurred on 12.07.2015 is not in dispute.
She further submits that P.W.1 in her evidence categorically stated that the said accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of unknown vehicle insured by the respondent No.2.
To substantiate the said aspect, the jurisdictional police also registered the case for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304-A of IPC and laid the charge sheet against the accused.

Though the police after investigation,
failed to trace out the vehicle and accused, the evidence of P.W.1 cannot be brushed aside.
Apart from that, the postmortem report of deceased also clearly NC: 2024:KHC-K:3855-DB discloses that the death of deceased is due to accidental injury.
In such circumstance, the Tribunal ought to have fastened the liability on the respondent No.2 and would have allowed the claim petition granting compensation.
On these grounds, she prays to allow the appeal.

10. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2-Insurance Company vehemently contend that, the Tribunal after considering the evidence and documents placed before it, the Tribunal rightly rejected the claim petition, which does not call for any interference.

He would further contend that though the accident in question is not in dispute, the Police have filed 'C' Final Report and it is clearly mentioned that both accused and vehicle have not been traced during the course of the investigation.
In such circumstance, in order to get compensation, the claim petition made by the petitioner is frivolous and false.

According to him, the vehicle in question and the insurance Smt.Akkamma Hugar vs Sri.Devaraj Shetty And Anr on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67106067/
3 policy is nowhere connected to the alleged incident.

sentences.text: As such, he prays to dismiss the appeal.
We have perused the records and considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.
12. The only point that arises for our consideration is:-
Whether the Tribunal is justified in rejecting the claim petition filed by the petitioner?

13. On careful perusal of the evidence and documents placed before the Tribunal, it could be seen that P.W.1 in her evidence deposed that on 12.07.2015 her deceased son Shravan Kumar along with his friend Muralidhar were proceeding on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-32/EE-3943 belonging to their company and a rider of unknown motorcycle dashed against their vehicle and due to said accident, her son deceased Sharavan Kumar sustained injuries and died on the spot.

P.W.1 no where in her evidence stated that the accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding by which vehicle and whether the said vehicle is covered with insurance policy NC: 2024:KHC-K:3855-DB by the respondent No.2.

Though the jurisdictional police investigated the case and laid the charge sheet,
the same disclose that both the accused and vehicle not traced during the course of the investigation.
In such circumstance, it is not forthcoming that how the respondent No.2 - Insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
In such circumstance, without any further discussion, we are of the considered view that the petitioner has tried to made a false and frivolous claim only in order to claim compensation.
As held by this Court in catena of decisions that, a false and frivolous claim should be curtailed.
14. In the light of above discussion, we are of the considered opinion that the Tribunal has rightly rejected the claim petition, which does not call for interference by this Court.

Accordingly, we answer the point raised in the Affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3855-DB ORDER i.
The appeal filed by the appellant/petitioner is dismissed.
ii. The judgment and award dated  24.07.2018 passed by the Tribunal  is confirmed.
